audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel / Shemuel Aleph chapter 28, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Philistine mobilization, David's ambiguous answer, Samuel's death, Saul's ban on mediums, En-dor terminology, disguise and coercion, woman's fear and recognition, Samuel apparition language, oracle, Amalek reference, Saul's collapse, fasting, and woman's meal.

verses.restored: In those days Philistines gathered their camps for army, to fight against Israel. Achish said to David, Know surely that with me you shall go out in camp, you and your men.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. And Achish said unto David, Know thou assuredly, that thou shalt go out with me to battle, thou and thy men.

modern.text: Now in those days the Philistines gathered their forces for warfare against Israel. So Achish said to David, “You must understand that you and your men are to go out to battle with me.”

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם וַיִּקְבְּצ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים אֶת מַֽחֲנֵיהֶם֙ לַצָּבָ֔א לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָכִישׁ֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּדַ֗ע כִּ֤י אִתִּי֙ תֵּצֵ֣א בַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה אַתָּ֖ה וַאֲנָשֶֽׁיךָ

verses.restored: David said to Achish, Therefore you shall know what your servant will do. Achish said to David, Therefore I will appoint you keeper of my head all days.

familiar.text: And David said to Achish, Surely thou shalt know what thy servant can do. And Achish said to David, Therefore will I make thee keeper of mine head for ever.

modern.text: David replied, “Then you will come to know what your servant can do.” “Very well,” said Achish. “I will make you my bodyguard for life.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל אָכִ֔ישׁ לָכֵן֙ אַתָּ֣ה תֵדַ֔ע אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָכִישׁ֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד לָכֵ֗ן שֹׁמֵ֧ר לְרֹאשִׁ֛י אֲשִֽׂימְךָ֖ כָּל הַיָּמִֽים

verses.restored: Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, in his city. Saul had removed mediums and spirit-knowers from land.

familiar.text: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. And Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land.

modern.text: Now by this time Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land.

original.text: וּשְׁמוּאֵ֣ל מֵ֔ת וַיִּסְפְּדוּ לוֹ֙ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בָרָמָ֖ה וּבְעִיר֑וֹ וְשָׁא֗וּל הֵסִ֛יר הָאֹב֥וֹת וְאֶת הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֖ים מֵהָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: Philistines gathered, came, and camped at Shunem. Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.

familiar.text: And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and pitched in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they pitched in Gilboa.

modern.text: The Philistines came together and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa.

original.text: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְשׁוּנֵ֑ם וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּגִּלְבֹּֽעַ

verses.restored: Saul saw camp of Philistines, and he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.

familiar.text: And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.

modern.text: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid and trembled violently.

original.text: וַיַּ֥רְא שָׁא֖וּל אֶת מַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיִּרָ֕א וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד לִבּ֖וֹ מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: Saul inquired of YHWH, but YHWH did not answer him, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.

familiar.text: And when Saul enquired of the LORD, the LORD answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.

modern.text: He inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets. Saul and the Medium of Endor

original.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל שָׁאוּל֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א עָנָ֖הוּ יְהוָ֑ה גַּ֧ם בַּחֲלֹמ֛וֹת גַּ֥ם בָּאוּרִ֖ים גַּ֥ם בַּנְּבִיאִֽם

verses.restored: Saul said to his servants, Seek for me a woman who is mistress of a familiar spirit, and I will go to her and inquire through her. His servants said to him, Look, there is a woman who is mistress of a familiar spirit at En-dor.

familiar.text: Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a woman that hath a familiar spirit at Endor.

modern.text: Then Saul said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so I can go and consult her.” “There is a medium at Endor,” his servants replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל לַעֲבָדָ֗יו בַּקְּשׁוּ לִי֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת בַּעֲלַת א֔וֹב וְאֵלְכָ֥ה אֵלֶ֖יהָ וְאֶדְרְשָׁה בָּ֑הּ וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ עֲבָדָיו֙ אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּ֛ה אֵ֥שֶׁת בַּֽעֲלַת א֖וֹב בְּעֵ֥ין דּֽוֹר

verses.restored: Saul disguised himself and put on other garments. He went, he and two men with him, and they came to woman by night. He said, Please divine for me by familiar spirit, and bring up for me whom I say to you.

familiar.text: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, I pray thee, divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto thee.

modern.text: So Saul disguised himself by putting on different clothes, and he set out with two of his men. They came to the woman at night, and Saul said, “Consult a spirit for me. Bring up for me the one I name.”

original.text: וַיִּתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ שָׁא֗וּל וַיִּלְבַּשׁ֙ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ ה֗וּא וּשְׁנֵ֤י אֲנָשִׁים֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל הָאִשָּׁ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר קסומי נָ֥א לִי֙ בָּא֔וֹב וְהַ֣עֲלִי לִ֔י אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר אֹמַ֖ר אֵלָֽיִךְ

verses.restored: The woman said to him, Look, you know what Saul has done, that he has cut off mediums and spirit-knowers from land. Why then are you setting a trap for my life, to cause me to die?

familiar.text: And the woman said unto him, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?

modern.text: But the woman replied, “Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has killed the mediums and spiritists in the land. Why have you set a trap to get me killed?”

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֣ה שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִכְרִ֛ית אֶת הָאֹב֥וֹת וְאֶת הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֖י מִן הָאָ֑רֶץ וְלָמָ֥ה אַתָּ֛ה מִתְנַקֵּ֥שׁ בְּנַפְשִׁ֖י לַהֲמִיתֵֽנִי

verses.restored: Saul swore to her by YHWH, saying, As YHWH lives, no guilt/punishment shall happen to you for this matter.

familiar.text: And Saul sware to her by the LORD, saying, As the LORD liveth, there shall no punishment happen to thee for this thing.

modern.text: Then Saul swore to her by the LORD: “As surely as the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this.”

original.text: וַיִּשָּׁ֤בַֽע לָהּ֙ שָׁא֔וּל בַּֽיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר חַי יְהוָ֕ה אִֽם יִקְּרֵ֥ךְ עָוֺ֖ן בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: The woman said, Whom shall I bring up for you? He said, Bring up Samuel for me.

familiar.text: Then said the woman, Whom shall I bring up unto thee? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.

modern.text: “Whom shall I bring up for you?” the woman asked. “Bring up Samuel,” he replied.

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה אֶת מִ֖י אַֽעֲלֶה לָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל הַֽעֲלִי לִֽי

verses.restored: The woman saw Samuel and cried with a great voice. The woman said to Saul, saying, Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!

familiar.text: And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice: and the woman spake to Saul, saying, Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul.

modern.text: But when the woman saw Samuel, she cried out in a loud voice and said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”

original.text: וַתֵּ֤רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶת שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַתִּזְעַ֖ק בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל וַתֹּאמֶר֩ הָאִשָּׁ֨ה אֶל שָׁא֧וּל לֵאמֹ֛ר לָ֥מָּה רִמִּיתָ֖נִי וְאַתָּ֥ה שָׁאֽוּל

verses.restored: King said to her, Do not fear. What did you see? The woman said to Saul, I saw a divine being/divinities ascending from earth.

familiar.text: And the king said unto her, Be not afraid: for what sawest thou? And the woman said unto Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.

modern.text: “Do not be afraid,” the king replied. “What do you see?” “I see a god coming up out of the earth,” the woman answered.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֥הּ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אַל תִּֽירְאִ֖י כִּ֣י מָ֣ה רָאִ֑ית וַתֹּ֤אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל אֱלֹהִ֥ים רָאִ֖יתִי עֹלִ֥ים מִן הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: He said to her, What is his form? She said, An old man is ascending, and he is wrapped in a robe. Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with face to ground and prostrated himself.

familiar.text: And he said unto her, What form is he of? And she said, An old man cometh up; and he is covered with a mantle. And Saul perceived that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself.

modern.text: “What does he look like?” asked Saul. “An old man is coming up,” she replied. “And he is wearing a robe.” So Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed facedown in reverence.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַֽה תָּאֳר֔וֹ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אִ֤ישׁ זָקֵן֙ עֹלֶ֔ה וְה֥וּא עֹטֶ֖ה מְעִ֑יל וַיֵּ֤דַע שָׁאוּל֙ כִּֽי שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל ה֔וּא וַיִּקֹּ֥ד אַפַּ֛יִם אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ

verses.restored: Samuel said to Saul, Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up? Saul said, I am greatly distressed. Philistines are fighting against me, Divine has turned aside from me and no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I called you to make known to me what I should do.

familiar.text: And Samuel said to Saul, Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God is departed from me, and answereth me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called thee, that thou mayest make known unto me what I shall do.

modern.text: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” “I am deeply distressed,” replied Saul. “The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל לָ֥מָּה הִרְגַּזְתַּ֖נִי לְהַעֲל֣וֹת אֹתִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁ֠אוּל צַר לִ֨י מְאֹ֜ד וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים נִלְחָמִ֣ים בִּ֗י וֵֽאלֹהִ֞ים סָ֤ר מֵֽעָלַי֙ וְלֹֽא עָנָ֣נִי ע֗וֹד גַּ֤ם בְּיַֽד הַנְּבִיאִם֙ גַּם בַּ֣חֲלֹמ֔וֹת וָאֶקְרָאֶ֣ה לְךָ֔ לְהוֹדִיעֵ֖נִי מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶֽׂה

verses.restored: Samuel said, Why do you ask me, since YHWH has turned aside from you and has become your adversary?

familiar.text: Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the LORD is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy?

modern.text: “Why do you consult me,” asked Samuel, “since the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy?

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וְלָ֖מָּה תִּשְׁאָלֵ֑נִי וַיהוָ֛ה סָ֥ר מֵעָלֶ֖יךָ וַיְהִ֥י עָרֶֽךָ

verses.restored: YHWH has done for YHWH-self as YHWH spoke by my hand: YHWH has torn kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David.

familiar.text: And the LORD hath done to him, as he spake by me: for the LORD hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David:

modern.text: He has done exactly what He spoke through me: The LORD has torn the kingship out of your hand and given it to your neighbor David.

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יְהוָה֙ ל֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר בְּיָדִ֑י וַיִּקְרַ֨ע יְהוָ֤ה אֶת הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מִיָּדֶ֔ךָ וַֽיִּתְּנָ֖הּ לְרֵעֲךָ֥ לְדָוִֽד

verses.restored: Because you did not listen to voice of YHWH and did not carry out burning anger against Amalek, therefore YHWH has done this thing to you this day.

familiar.text: Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the LORD, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the LORD done this thing unto thee this day.

modern.text: Because you did not obey the LORD or carry out His burning anger against Amalek, the LORD has done this to you today.

original.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא שָׁמַ֨עְתָּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹֽא עָשִׂ֥יתָ חֲרוֹן אַפּ֖וֹ בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק עַל כֵּן֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה עָשָֽׂה לְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: YHWH will also give Israel with you into hand of Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. YHWH will also give camp of Israel into hand of Philistines.

familiar.text: Moreover the LORD will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me: the LORD also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.

modern.text: Moreover, the LORD will deliver Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. And the LORD will deliver the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.”

original.text: וְיִתֵּ֣ן יְ֠הוָה גַּ֣ם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל עִמְּךָ֙ בְּיַד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמָחָ֕ר אַתָּ֥ה וּבָנֶ֖יךָ עִמִּ֑י גַּ֚ם אֶת מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יִתֵּ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: Saul hurried and fell full length to ground and was greatly afraid because of words of Samuel. There was no strength in him, because he had eaten no bread all day and all night.

familiar.text: Then Saul fell straightway all along on the earth, and was sore afraid, because of the words of Samuel: and there was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night.

modern.text: Immediately Saul fell flat on the ground, terrified by the words of Samuel. And his strength was gone, because he had not eaten anything all that day and night.

original.text: וַיְמַהֵ֣ר שָׁא֗וּל וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מְלֹא קֽוֹמָתוֹ֙ אַ֔רְצָה וַיִּרָ֥א מְאֹ֖ד מִדִּבְרֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל גַּם כֹּ֨חַ֙ לֹא הָ֣יָה ב֔וֹ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אָכַל֙ לֶ֔חֶם כָּל הַיּ֖וֹם וְכָל הַלָּֽיְלָה

verses.restored: The woman came to Saul and saw that he was greatly terrified. She said to him, Look, your maidservant listened to your voice. I placed my life in my palm and listened to your words that you spoke to me.

familiar.text: And the woman came unto Saul, and saw that he was sore troubled, and said unto him, Behold, thine handmaid hath obeyed thy voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have hearkened unto thy words which thou spakest unto me.

modern.text: When the woman came to Saul and saw how distraught he was, she said to him, “Look, your maidservant has obeyed your voice. I took my life in my hands and did as you told me.

original.text: וַתָּב֤וֹא הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל וַתֵּ֖רֶא כִּי נִבְהַ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה שָׁמְעָ֤ה שִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֙ בְּקוֹלֶ֔ךָ וָאָשִׂ֤ים נַפְשִׁי֙ בְּכַפִּ֔י וָֽאֶשְׁמַע֙ אֶת דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ אֵלָֽי

verses.restored: Now please, you also listen to voice of your maidservant. Let me set before you a morsel of bread, and eat, so there may be strength in you when you go on way.

familiar.text: Now therefore, I pray thee, hearken thou also unto the voice of thine handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before thee; and eat, that thou mayest have strength, when thou goest on thy way.

modern.text: Now please listen to your servant and let me set a morsel of bread before you so you may eat and have the strength to go on your way.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁמַֽע נָ֤א גַם אַתָּה֙ בְּק֣וֹל שִׁפְחָתֶ֔ךָ וְאָשִׂ֧מָה לְפָנֶ֛יךָ פַּת לֶ֖חֶם וֶאֱכ֑וֹל וִיהִ֤י בְךָ֙ כֹּ֔חַ כִּ֥י תֵלֵ֖ךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ

verses.restored: He refused and said, I will not eat. But his servants, and also woman, pressed him. He listened to their voice, arose from ground, and sat upon bed.

familiar.text: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, compelled him; and he hearkened unto their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat upon the bed.

modern.text: Saul refused, saying, “I will not eat.” But his servants joined the woman in urging him, and he heeded their voice. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed.

original.text: וַיְמָאֵ֗ן וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֹכַ֔ל וַיִּפְרְצוּ ב֤וֹ עֲבָדָיו֙ וְגַם הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע לְקֹלָ֑ם וַיָּ֨קָם֙ מֵֽהָאָ֔רֶץ וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב אֶל הַמִּטָּֽה

verses.restored: The woman had a fattened calf in house. She hurried and slaughtered it, took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread.

familiar.text: And the woman had a fat calf in the house; and she hasted, and killed it, and took flour, and kneaded it, and did bake unleavened bread thereof:

modern.text: The woman had a fattened calf at her house, and she quickly slaughtered it. She also took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread.

original.text: וְלָאִשָּׁ֤ה עֵֽגֶל מַרְבֵּק֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת וַתְּמַהֵ֖ר וַתִּזְבָּחֵ֑הוּ וַתִּקַּח קֶ֣מַח וַתָּ֔לָשׁ וַתֹּפֵ֖הוּ מַצּֽוֹת

verses.restored: She brought it before Saul and before his servants, and they ate. They arose and went in that night.

familiar.text: And she brought it before Saul, and before his servants; and they did eat. Then they rose up, and went away that night.

modern.text: She served it to Saul and his servants, and they ate. And that night they got up and left.

original.text: וַתַּגֵּ֧שׁ לִפְנֵֽי שָׁא֛וּל וְלִפְנֵ֥י עֲבָדָ֖יו וַיֹּאכֵ֑לוּ וַיָּקֻ֥מוּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַהֽוּא

translation_notes: The woman of En-dor is neither named nor demonized by the narrator. She is criminalized by Saul, deceived by him, placed at lethal risk, and then becomes the person who feeds him.
This chapter must never support witch-hunts, violence against spiritual practitioners, misogyny, antisemitic occult stereotypes, or coercive religious policing.
The text presents an extraordinary narrative event but does not provide a safe method for contacting the dead or authorize attempts to reproduce the scene.
Saul's fear, collapse, fasting, and terror are not moral failures or evidence of demonic possession. Acute distress requires care, food, safety, and support.

The woman's compliance occurs under disguise, royal power, two male companions, criminal penalty, and an oath from the person who made the law. It cannot be treated as freely negotiated professional consent.
The oracle repeats the Amalek rationale from chapter 15. That genocide command remains ethically dangerous and cannot be used to blame Saul for mercy or to justify modern violence.
'Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me' predicts death without describing eternal destiny or endorsing suicide.
The woman's meal is embodied care offered across religious, political, and legal hostility. Her humanity should remain central.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not use this chapter to teach spirit-contact procedures, persecute mediums or occult practitioners, or diagnose distress as demonic. Do not shame Saul for terror or fasting. Center the unnamed woman's vulnerability, deception, courage, boundaries, and care; she is endangered by the king and still preserves his life for the night.
